It is further submitted that there has been no progress in the trial, as not a single witness has been examined till date and even summons have not been served upon the witnesses.
It is also submitted that there is an unexplained delay in lodging the FIR.
Moreover, there is no medical evidence or independent eyewitness to corroborate the allegations of sexual assault made by the appellant.
It is further submitted that the appellant is in custody since 04.06.2025.
He is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
In view of the aforesaid submissions, it is prayed that the appellant may be released on bail on the ground of delay in trial.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the appeal for bail and submitted that the present second appeal has been filed without any substantial change in circumstances since the dismissal of the first appeal.

It is pointed out that the order-sheets filed along with the application (I.A. No. 28030 of 2025) indicate that the matter was listed on 26.09.2025 for fixation of the trial programme and thereafter the case was fixed for prosecution evidence on 06.11.2025 and 24.11.2025; however, no further order-sheets have been placed on record.
In the absence of any material change in circumstances, it is contended that the second appeal for bail is not maintainable.
In view of the aforesaid, the appeal filed on behalf of appellant deserves to be dismissed.

6. Having considered the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perused the documents placed on record and keeping in view the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds that no substantial change in circumstances warranting reconsideration of the prayer NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:62815 3 CRA-10581-2025 for bail in this second appeal.
No new material has been brought on record to justify a different view at this stage.
Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is not inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the appellant.
7. Accordingly, the criminal appeal for bail stands dismissed.
